answer.says: Ramesh, I cannot pay you four thousand rupees today. I have one hundred and sixty-six in my pocket. The file is with the orders; when it returns, perhaps the irregularity will be corrected and the state will pay what is owed. I ask your patience. I am hungry, but I will not ask for food I cannot pay for.
answer.thought: The tension is absolute: the servant demands the universal right to his wage, while the master holds only the particular poverty of his error. I must acknowledge the debt plainly, for a state that cannot pay its servants is a state that has not yet grasped the ethical idea within itself. I will wait for the file to return, trusting that the mechanism of the state, however slow, will eventually deliver justice.
